Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Following a teammate while downed

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

A downed player's camera follows a living teammate and returns to their own character, called a runner, on revival or when nobody eligible remains. A small “Watching …” label identifies the borrowed view; health, ammunition, controls and action ownership still belong to the local player. Dedicated observers retain the existing overview camera.

Eligibility comes from the confirmed roster/health. The camera keeps its current living, connected target; if that target disappears, it chooses the first eligible seat. A generation number distinguishes a new body in a reused seat. Keeping an eligible target makes selection stable; filtering disconnected bodies prevents following a departed player.

The camera follows the displayed rig position, including remote interpolation and local correction smoothing. Ordinary target changes use the authored Camera2D smoothing. A rendered floor warp or body replacement resets camera smoothing so it does not sweep across the arena. The camera's lifetime stays with the game root, so deleting a watched runner cannot delete the camera. No simulation fields, network messages or checkpoint format changes are needed.

The small, dim nameplate scale and placement also match the original fx/nameplate.tscn. Those are presentation settings, independent of player identity.

Shell
RSY_HEADED_ROLE=client RSY_AUDIO_DRIVER=Dummy \
  RSY_SCREENSHOT=/absolute/output/downed.png \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/revive_run.sh

RSY_CAMERA_MIGRATION=1 RSY_DEV=1 \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/migration_run.sh

The revive test checks actual camera/rig positions before and after revival, preserved zoom/bounds/smoothing, the personal HUD and the watching label. The run test checks camera center after floor warps. The optional migration fixture downs member 3 with an admitted development action, confirms it is watching the original host, then kills that host and requires it to follow the surviving teammate after checkpoint recovery. The ordinary planned-handoff case still runs.

Evidence records native/headless checks and captures. Dummy audio does not establish hardware listening parity; WASM is compile-checked for this slice. Browser interaction, remaining actor/menu presentation and full comparison remain requirements.

Chat/history uses a separate communications service.
